scheme_name: National Rubber Policy for MSME Manufacturers
overview: The National Rubber Policy for MSME Manufacturers is a scheme by the Rubber Board, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, aimed at supporting MSME manufacturers in the rubber and plastics sector through financial assistance and other benefits. The scheme is part of the Rubber Board's initiatives to support the rubber industry, including financial assistance for MSME manufacturers. The policy is implemented by the Rubber Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, with applications processed through the Rubber Board's financial assistance schemes.
objectives: To provide financial assistance to MSME manufacturers in the rubber and plastics sector
To support the growth and competitiveness of MSME manufacturers in the rubber industry
To promote value addition and value of rubber products
To support the rubber sector through financial assistance
To enhance the competitiveness of Indian rubber products in domestic and international markets
eligibility: MSME manufacturers engaged in the manufacturing of rubber and rubber products are eligible to apply for financial assistance under the Rubber Board's schemes. Applicants must be registered as MSMEs under the MSMED Act, 2006, and must be engaged in the manufacturing of rubber products. The scheme is open to MSMEs across India engaged in rubber processing, manufacturing, and value addition.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of subsidies or grants for MSME manufacturers in the rubber sector. Benefits include support for technology upgradation, quality improvement, market development, and value addition in rubber processing. The scheme also provides support for participation in trade fairs, exhibitions, and buyer-seller meets to enhance market access. Additionally, assistance may be provided for setting up processing units, adopting modern technologies, and improving product quality and competitiveness.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as subsidies or grants to eligible MSME manufacturers for specific activities such as technology upgradation, quality improvement, market development, and setting up processing units. The exact quantum of support varies based on the nature of the project and the beneficiary's eligibility, subject to the guidelines of the Rubber Board's financial assistance schemes. The support is typically disbursed after verification of project completion and submission of required documents.
application_process: 1. Visit the Rubber Board's official website or contact the Rubber Board office for information on available schemes. 2. Check eligibility criteria for the specific scheme under the National Rubber Policy for MSME Manufacturers. 3. Prepare the required documents including MSME registration, project report, quotations, and other relevant documents. 4. Submit the application form along with required documents to the Rubber Board office or through the designated portal. 5. The application will be reviewed by the Rubber Board's technical and financial committees. 6. Upon approval, financial assistance will be disbursed as per the scheme guidelines. 7. Submit utilization reports and other required documents after project completion.
required_documents: Project report detailing the proposed activity
Quotations for equipment or services to be procured
Proof of land/premises ownership or lease agreement
Balance sheet and income tax returns of the business
Any other documents as specified by the Rubber Board for the specific scheme
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Rubber Board, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
caveats: Financial assistance is subject to availability of funds under the scheme
Beneficiaries must utilize the funds strictly for the approved purpose
Utilization certificates and audited statements must be submitted after project completion
The Rubber Board reserves the right to reject applications that do not meet scheme guidelines
Assistance may be withdrawn if funds are misutilized or if project milestones are not met
